_meta.purpose: Material property library for the strain-analyzer agent. Values are conservative literature/manufacturer figures for as-printed FDM parts on a Bambu X1C; treat them as engineering estimates, not certified test data. Per-design overrides live in spec.json.loadCase.materialOverride.
_meta.convention: FDM parts are anisotropic. `yield_MPa` is the in-plane (XY) tensile yield; `interlayer_derate` is the multiplier to apply when stress is normal to the layer plane (Z-tension). Bending stress at a section with layer lines parallel to the bending axis pulls on layer interfaces — apply the derate. Bending stress with layer lines perpendicular to the bending axis is in-plane — don't derate.
_meta.sources: Yield/tensile from Bambu Lab material profile cards (PLA Basic, PLA-CF, PETG-HF) and published filament datasheets (Polymaker PolyMax PLA-CF, Prusament PETG). Interlayer derate from independent FDM strength studies — values in the 0.45-0.70 range across PLA/PLA-CF/PETG, with CF the weakest because fiber alignment is in-plane only.

PLA.notes: Bambu PLA Basic profile yield ~50 MPa as-printed. Brittle failure; design to yield, not ultimate.

PLA-CF.notes: Bambu/Polymaker PLA-CF. ~40% stiffer than PLA but interlayer adhesion is the weak link — fibers reinforce in-plane only. Treat as more brittle than PLA in bending across layers.

PETG.notes: More ductile than PLA; better interlayer adhesion. Lower stiffness — deflection-limited designs may need thicker sections.
